mechanism_narrative: The latest bounce in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT after several weak weeks signals more commuting and downtown circulation, which raises retail-and-recreation visits within the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -38.1 to -31.3 then -32.4 while TRANSIT improved from -34.9 to -30.3 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay at or below their t-0w levels for the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC should not exceed its prior four-week mean; a sustained decline would reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL time after a weak mobility week reflects more at-home substitution and less discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises by at least 1 point week-on-week after a prior week of elevated at-home staying
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 7.7 at t-1w and 5.9 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved only modestly from -38.6 to -35.0
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues rising but RETAIL_REC is flat or higher over the following two weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM strengthens at the same time as PARKS turn positive, weekday out-of-home trip bundling expands neighborhood activity and pulls retail visits up over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved to -24.6 and PARKS jumped to 5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS remain negative or GROCERY_PHARM falls back below the t-1w level while RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to its last four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A transit deterioration threshold captures a restriction or service shock: once TRANSIT falls below -35, access to shopping districts weakens and RETAIL_REC drops within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses below -35 after having been above that level in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged from -34.9 to -30.3 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below -35 and RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next week, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-weekend visitation pattern, a rebound in PARKS precedes a short spillover into retail districts, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks when weather is favorable.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive after at least one negative week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -18.7 at t-1w to 5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays positive for one week but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next two weeks, the spillover claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates coordinated return-to-office movement, which produces a lagged lift in retail-and-recreation mobility over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises but TRANSIT does not improve in the same window, RETAIL_REC should not be expected to rise; persistence of weak retail would reject the interaction.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM falls while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, households consolidate trips and substitute away from discretionary shopping, reducing RETAIL_REC over one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines for two consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained negative throughout the snapshot and RESIDENTIAL stayed positive
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM declines for two weeks but RETAIL_REC holds steady or increases, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, improving TRANSIT combined with a stable or rising WORKPLACES series leads retail mobility to recover, because more workers can access central shopping corridors after commuting hours.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -34.1 to -30.3 at t-0w while WORKPLACES stayed near -32 to -34
failure_condition: If reopening continues but TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weaken, RETAIL_REC should not rise; a lower or unchanged retail mean would reject the claim.
